items.title: David Byrne Returns to Oscar Race With Original Song for Elon Musk Documentary ‘Musk’ (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary:
David Byrne wrote and performs an original song for "Musk," Alex Gibney's 235-minute documentary about Elon Musk. The track, "Let Me Sell You a Dream," was co-written with the film's composer Daniel Pemberton and plays inside the film, which Bleecker Street opens in U.S. theaters on Oct. 16. Variety reported the song exclusively, along with the news that it will be entered in the best original song race at the 2027 Oscars.

Byrne said the lyrics came almost entirely secondhand. "I asked for good quotes from the Martian, and found more of them online," he said. "I'm sure he loves dropping these wild statements, and those became the lyrics. All his own words. No editorializing. Straight from the man's mouth to mine."

Gibney, who directs and produces, said he had wanted Byrne on the film for a while. "My wife and I were at the Pantages for the filming of Stop Making Sense, so I sensed that he would find a musical way into what the film is trying to say," he said, describing the finished song as "extremely hard core, foot-tapping sardonic poetry."

A nomination would return Byrne to the Oscars for the first time since 1988, when he won best original score for "The Last Emperor" alongside Ryuichi Sakamoto and Cong Su. Pemberton, his collaborator here, was nominated for best original song in 2021 for "Hear My Voice," written with Celeste for "The Trial of the Chicago 7," and also scored "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse."

Gibney first said in March 2023 that he was months into production on the documentary. Musk predicted on X that the result would be a "hit-piece," and Gibney answered on the same platform: "how would you know?" The film, which Gibney has called a definitive and unvarnished portrait, premieres out of competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on Sept. 8 before playing Toronto.

Jessie Deeter and Erin Edeiken produce for Jigsaw Productions, with Dana O'Keefe for Double Agent, Joey Marra and Zhang Xin for Closer Media, and Nick Shumaker and Jessica Grimshaw for Anonymous Content. Ronan Farrow and Lawrence Wright also produce. At just under four hours, it is among the longest films Gibney has made.

items.title: Travis Kelce Opens Up About Taylor Swift Wedding, Adam Sandler’s Role in Ceremony
items.summary:
Travis Kelce spoke publicly about his wedding to Taylor Swift for the first time on a new episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother Jason. The couple married at Madison Square Garden in a private ceremony on July 3, 2026, and had said almost nothing about it since, releasing no official photographs.

Kelce described the night as "insane, it was a night I'll never forget," and said he and Swift were grateful to everyone who attended. "From the vows to seeing everyone and how much fun we had that evening, and hearing that being relayed through everyone's stories of that night. It was just magical, man. I wish it could have lasted longer than that. Once the drinks got served, everyone started to mosey out."

He also explained the choice of venue, which struck some as an unusual setting for a private wedding. The pair wanted "somewhere where we could have an intimate and genuine setting without a lot of distractions," he said, adding that "we needed to have a private feel, and MSG went above and beyond to give us that."

The most concrete new detail, as Consequence noted in its account of the episode, concerned the officiant. Kelce revealed that Adam Sandler got ordained in New York specifically to marry them, and praised the way he handled it: "The way he did it, in the very Sand-man style, and giving us more than what we could've imagined at that moment, knowing that it was the biggest night of our lives, it was absolutely insane."

Kelce said the ceremony was phone-free, which he credited for the tone of the evening. "With no phones, people not having to be on guard, it makes everyone be in the moment and present," he said, describing friends from his childhood mixing with Swift's family, friends and colleagues. "We wanted it to be a beautiful ceremony and made sure everyone left there having some fun."

items.title: ‘S.W.A.T. Exiles’ Trailer: Shemar Moore’s Hondo Is Out For One Last Shot At Redemption In Starz Spinoff
items.summary:
Starz has released the trailer for S.W.A.T. Exiles, the spinoff of the long-running procedural, ahead of a September 25 premiere. Shemar Moore returns as LAPD S.W.A.T. Sergeant Daniel "Hondo" Harrelson, the role he played on the original series.

The premise puts Hondo out of the job first. A botched raid kills a young operator, Nico Reyes, and Hondo leaves the work he has built his life around until his former commanding officer Robert Hicks, played again by Patrick St. Esprit, hands him one last assignment: assemble a new S.W.A.T. unit out of the department's most talented rejects.

That squad includes Sammy Bishop (Lucy Barrett), a gun-show influencer with something to prove; Ethan Cole (Freddy Miyares), a socially awkward tactical savant; Cassidy Reed (Zyra Gorecki), guarded and out to earn her place; Jude Callan (Ronen Rubinstein), a wildcard with a troubled past; and Malik Anderson (Adain Bradley), ambitious and concealing plenty. As Deadline described the season, the team works cartel assassins and gun-runners while Hondo becomes convinced someone inside the unit is leaking to outside interests, part of a broader effort to dismantle S.W.A.T. and replace it with something private and less accountable.

Sony Pictures Television commissioned the series. Jason Ning, previously of Lucifer and Mrs. Davis, serves as showrunner and executive producer alongside Neal H. Moritz, Pavun Shetty, Moore, James Scura and Jon Cowan.

The season builds toward a reckoning that the network says will decide the futures of Hondo and his team as well as the unit itself. S.W.A.T. Exiles arrives on Starz on September 25.

items.title: Blackpink and ‘White Lotus’ Star Lisa Documentary ‘Always Lalisa’ Sets Global Release
items.summary:
Sony Music Vision has set a global release for Always Lalisa, a feature documentary about Blackpink member Lisa. Directed by Sue Kim, the film opens in Imax and conventional cinemas worldwide for a limited engagement beginning Oct. 12, with Trafalgar Releasing handling theatrical distribution, before moving to YouTube Premium as an exclusive streaming release later in 2026.

The documentary covers a pivotal year in which Lisa stepped away from Blackpink for the first time since childhood, building a solo career and acting work while attempting to keep some private life intact. It premieres at the 2026 Toronto Film Festival ahead of the theatrical run, according to Variety.

Sony Music Vision president Tom Mackay said the company hoped the film would create the same connection as Lisa's music, and Trafalgar chief executive Marc Allenby called it "an unguarded look at Lisa's path from Blackpink stardom to global recognition." Lyor Cohen, YouTube's global head of music, framed the streaming release as a natural fit, saying it gives "her millions of fans a front-row seat to her evolution as an artist."

The film lands during an unusually crowded stretch for Lisa. She performed "Goals" with Anitta and Rema at the 2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony, played Coachella 2025 as a solo act, joined the 2026 Met Gala host committee and presented at the 2026 Golden Globes. She made her acting debut as Mook in HBO's The White Lotus and has two Netflix projects moving, the action film Tygo and an untitled romantic comedy.

Her EP Press Play arrives Oct. 23, led by the single "SaWaDika" on Sept. 3. She also became the first K-pop artist with a Las Vegas residency: four Viva La Lisa shows at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace on Nov. 13-14 and Nov. 27-28, which sold out in under 10 minutes.

Sony Music Vision produces with RCA Records and Tremolo Productions, in association with Salt Water Productions and Lloud Co. Kim produces with Courtney Crockett, while Morgan Neville and Caitrin Rogers executive produce for Tremolo.

items.title: Alanis Morissette Accuses Ex-Tour Manager of Extortion Scheme in Lawsuit
items.summary:
Alanis Morissette has sued her former tour manager in California federal court, accusing her of an extortion scheme built around threats of drug trafficking allegations. The complaint, filed Tuesday, names Keren Urinov, who managed Morissette's 2025 European tour, and brings claims of extortion, fraud and negligent misrepresentation.

According to the filing, British airport authorities arrested Urinov in 2025 while Morissette and her crew were flying from the U.K. to Spain for a show. Urinov later told Morissette that officials had flagged a bag containing marijuana, which she carried under an Israeli medical permit, along with xylazine, an animal tranquilizer that is also used illicitly.

The lawsuit says Urinov also told Morissette during the tour that she had once been arrested in Latin America for smuggling drugs inside a surfboard and had fled authorities. The complaint calls that a shock, since Urinov had said before being hired that nothing in her past would complicate touring. Afterward, the filing alleges, Urinov and her attorney sent escalating letters threatening to report drug trafficking charges against Morissette to U.K. police unless the singer signed her to a 15-year contract with annual raises and bonuses and hired an immigration attorney to secure her U.S. work authorization.

"Morissette brings this lawsuit reluctantly," the complaint says. "But Morissette will not agree to work with an incompetent blackmailer for the next fifteen years or pay her a ransom under the gun." The filing also faults Urinov's job performance, claiming a hotel booking error cost Morissette $70,000. Morissette is seeking more than $75,000 in repayment plus punitive damages, and has requested a jury trial.

Law360 reported that Urinov previously worked as an executive at Live Nation's Israeli unit and has filed her own suit against Morissette in British court, though the substance of those allegations was not clear. Morissette plays Riot Fest in Chicago on Sept. 18 and has four November dates at the YouTube Theater in Los Angeles.
